rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when the person seems pitiable or generally unfortunate.

example.english: They are truly hapless, being ill while also having to look after two children.
example.traditional: 佢一個人病住，仲要照顧兩個細路，真係可憐。
example.jyutping: keoi5 jat1 go3 jan4 bing6 zyu6 zung6 jiu3 ziu3 gu3 loeng5 go3 sai3 lou6 zan1 hai6 ho2 lin4

rows.note: Use this when the misfortune is specifically understood as bad luck, especially for events or circumstances.

example.english: We were hapless to run into a typhoon on this trip.
example.traditional: 今次旅行遇着打風，我哋真係唔好彩。
example.jyutping: gam1 ci3 leoi5 hang4 jyu6 zoek6 daa2 fung1 ngo5 dei6 zan1 hai6 m4 hou2 coi2

rows.note: Use this colloquial choice for a person who is persistently or conspicuously unlucky.

example.english: They are really hapless; their new phone broke on the second day.
example.traditional: 佢真係黑仔，買部新電話第二日就壞咗。
example.jyutping: keoi5 zan1 hai6 hak1 zai2 maai5 bou6 san1 din6 waa2 dai6 ji6 jat6 zau6 waai6 zo2
